metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Iceland

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD PISA 2022 factsheet reports descriptive and comparative results for the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment in Iceland. The underlying PISA microdata are collected using a complex, multi-stage sampling design across schools and students, and OECD/PISA analyses are typically conducted with sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the specific weighting implementation cannot be confirmed from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported differences and uncertainty statements (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicate that the analysis accounts for sampling uncertainty, but the exact weighting/replication details are deferred to the PISA technical documentation and reader’s guide referenced by the report.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This factsheet is a descriptive country profile and does not report an explicit student-level predictive model or a documented plausible-values (PV) estimation procedure for a specific outcome. While PISA achievement reporting is typically based on PVs, the provided text does not state how PVs were handled for the reported creative thinking scale and related comparisons. Missing-data handling is therefore not documented in the excerpt, and the absence should be treated as a reporting gap for methodological replication rather than evidence that missingness was absent.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The Iceland analytic sample reported in the factsheet consists of 3,360 students in 134 schools who completed the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking assessment in the context of the mathematics, reading, or science assessment administration (reported as representing about 4,400 15-year-olds). The excerpt does not describe additional exclusions (e.g., missing questionnaire items or partial test completion) beyond the fact that students completed the assessment.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III factsheet summarizes Iceland’s performance on the PISA 2022 Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-old students. The creative thinking assessment includes 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes—generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, and evaluating and improving ideas—across four domain contexts: written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, and scientific problem solving. Iceland’s mean creative thinking score is 30/60, significantly below the OECD average of 33. The factsheet also reports proficiency distribution: 72% of students reach at least Level 3 (baseline), and 21% are top performers at Levels 5–6. Within Iceland, socio-economic status is a strong predictor (explaining 11% of variation), and girls outperform boys by 4.7 score points. The excerpt provides uncertainty statements (95% confidence intervals) and notes COVID-19-related data collection challenges and sampling-standard caveats for some countries/economies, but it does not provide the underlying PV/missing-data/weighting procedures needed for full methodological replication.
